reason: README gives a pip-installable `protenix pred` CLI that runs structure prediction from a JSON file with public weights, feasible on CPU for a small protein without MSA.
demo: README 'Quick Prediction': protenix pred -i examples/input.json -o ./output -n protenix_base_default_v1.0.0
goal: Install Protenix (CPU only, no GPU) so that `protenix pred -i <input.json> -o <outdir> -n protenix_base_default_v1.0.0 --use_msa false -d fp32 -c 4 -p 20 -e 1` works on a small single-chain protein JSON (format like examples/input.json) and writes predicted structure .cif files plus confidence json under the output directory. Model weights are downloaded automatically; avoid anything needing GPU-only kernels. Provide /work/env.sh (activating the environment) and make the command work from /work/Protenix.
check: The hidden test runs protenix pred on a 76-residue protein and verifies a predicted mmCIF with plausible atom count and a confidence summary json are produced.
